description: Solo engineering student from ENSA Oujda, Morocco (Electronic, Computer & Network Systems), building LUNA-CTRL: a lunar outpost game for kids aged 7-12. Players balance power, oxygen and radiation shielding and learn every choice has a cost. Skills: Python, embedded/IoT, web.
summary: LUNA-CTRL is a 5-day Moon base survival game for kids aged 7 to 12. Players command a Moon base while a real solar storm from 8 to 12 May 2024 hits, using archived NASA DONKI flare data. Every choice has a cost: power spent on the shield is power not spent on air. It addresses the “Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge by teaching real engineering trade-offs, radiation risk and communication delay through play, with a friendly mascot explaining why each result happened. It matters because it makes space science feel like decision-making, not memorizing.
details: Each day a player sees the real solar report for that date (flare count and strongest class), handles 2 to 4 events with two costly options each, picks 2 base actions, and then faces the storm, whose strength comes from the day’s real strongest flare. A new factor unlocks each day (power and air, shielding, food, communication delay), so children learn one idea at a time. After every event, three short cards explain what changed, why, and a space fact. There are three levels (Junior ages 7 to 9, Commander 10 to 12, Expert family) with different event counts, storm strength and decision timers. Difficulty was tuned with thousands of simulated games using random, careful and reckless players, and the game rules have automatic tests. Music and effects are synthesized in the browser and can be muted. Built with Python and Streamlit. Limitations: flare class stands in for the whole storm, and all resource numbers and the Earth delay are simplified for gameplay.
projectRefs: None used beyond NASA DONKI. Reference concepts: lunar regolith shielding, Earth-Moon radio delay (about 1.3 s).
